newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MMC raises stake in Berjuntai.
newsitem.headline: MMC raises stake in Berjuntai.

text.p: Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd (MMC) said on Tuesday it was proposing to increase its stake in Berjuntai Tin Dredging Bhd to 43.25 percent from the present 28.64 percent.
Engineering services firm MMC said in a statement issued by its merchant bankers that it plans to buy 28.86 million new Berjuntai shares for 129.88 million ringgit.
The proposed acquisition will maintain MMC as Berjuntai's largest shareholder and will trigger a mandatory general offer for the remaining Berjuntai shares.
MMC said it will finance the proposed purchase from internally generated funds.
Berjuntai is involved in mining operations and on Tuesday announced a plan to diversify into cement production by acquisition of two private firms.
In a separate statement, Berjuntai said it plans to buy the entire equity of Kesabah Holdings Sdn Bhd and Batuluga Sdn Bhd for 179.1 million ringgit.
Kesabah and Batuluga have bought equities in a company has interests in a cement production plant and another which plans to build a clinker plant in eastern Sabah state.
At the end of the exercise, Berjuntai will own a 65 percent stake in cement production firm, Cement Industries (Sabah) Sdn Bhd, which has a 500,000-tonne per annum plant in Sabah.
Berjuntai will also own 61 percent in Padu-Wangsa Sdn Bhd, which plans to build a clinker facility. No details were given on the facility except that earthworks on the project has started.
Berjuntai will pay for the Kesabah and Batuluga purchases by issuing 59.7 million new shares at 3.0 ringgit each. Berjuntai stock closed at 15.80 cents on Tuesday, up 60 cents.
MMC stock closed at 7.40 ringgit, down 30 cents.
